items.title: ㅐ vs ㅔ in one song — two shapes, one sound! 애 에 개 게 #learnkorean
items.text:
Sing along with Mongle — ㅐ and ㅔ look different, but they sound the same: “e”.

Add one stick and the sound changes:
아 → 애 · 어 → 에
가 → 개 · 거 → 게 · 나 → 내 · 너 → 네 · 사 → 새 · 서 → 세

모양만 달라, 둘 다 에! (moyangman dalla, dul da e!) — only the shape is different, both say “e”!
"이건 뭐?" (What is this?) — 개 (dog) and 게 (crab) sound exactly the same; the spelling tells them apart.
Then say hello politely — 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo) — and answer 네! (ne — yes!).

Romanization appears under every letter: ㅐ is written “ae” and ㅔ “e” — different spelling, same sound, just like in Hangul.
English captions (CC) have the lyrics.
At the end, try reading 배 · 카페 · 메뉴 (boat · café · menu).

Hangul for Beginners · 한글 초보단계 #6 — after the vowel (#1), consonant (#2), batchim (#3), double-vowel (#4) and first-words (#5) songs.
SYNK LAB · learn Korean the fun way, with Mongle.
#learnkorean #hangul #koreanvowels
alt: A felt kid and the coral felt mascot Mongle learn ㅐ and ㅔ: a blue stick slides in next to 아 to make 애 and next to 어 to make 에, the kid cups his ears for the “e” sound every time, a bracket joins 애 and 에 into one speaker icon, and a felt puppy (개) and crab (게) show two words that sound the same — under a white card reading “Two shapes, one sound!”
